How we work

What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 01

    1–2 weeks

    Discover

    We map how orders, listings and conversations actually flow today across channels, the OMS, couriers, the helpdesk and consent records. We sample orders, RTO and NDR history, return reasons and support tickets to find where money and time leak, and agree which journey to fix first.

    Deliverables

    • Current-state map of channels, systems and handoffs
    • Leak analysis from order, RTO, NDR, return and ticket samples
    • Prioritized automation backlog with owners
    • Consent and data inventory for messaging

    What we need from you

    • Read access to the storefront, OMS and courier aggregator
    • Sample exports of orders, returns and support tickets
    • Current return, refund, cancellation and warranty policies
    • Named owners for operations, CX and catalog decisions
  2. 02

    1–2 weeks

    Design

    We design each flow end to end: triggers, rules, message templates, review queues and data handling. Templates are drafted for WhatsApp category approval and DLT registration, discount and urgency wording is checked against the dark-pattern guidelines, and every decision point names the person who owns it.

    Deliverables

    • Flow designs with triggers, rules and exception paths
    • Message templates ready for WhatsApp approval and DLT registration
    • Human checkpoint and escalation matrix
    • Measurement plan with holdouts and KPI definitions

    What we need from you

    • Approval of templates, tone and offers
    • Consent and opt-in wording reviewed by the client's legal or compliance owner
    • Business rules for COD, returns, exchanges and price changes
  3. 03

    2–5 weeks

    Build

    We build in short increments on the agreed stack, usually n8n or Node.js workflows, a Supabase data layer, Retool review consoles and the client's existing messaging providers. Integrations use official APIs, credentials are kept in a secrets vault, and every workflow logs what it did and why.

    Deliverables

    • Working workflows and integrations in a staging environment
    • Review consoles for held orders, claims and approvals
    • AI prompts, retrieval indexes and evaluation sets where AI is used
    • Monitoring, alerting and run logs

    What we need from you

    • API credentials for sandbox and production accounts
    • WhatsApp Business account and Solution Provider access
    • Test orders, SKUs and courier test accounts
  4. 04

    1–2 weeks

    Validate & launch

    We test normal and failure paths with realistic orders: undelivered messages, courier API errors, partial stock, wrong addresses and opt-outs. AI answers are scored against approved sources. Launch is staged by channel, pincode set or share of orders, with a rollback switch, and avoids peak sale days.

    Deliverables

    • Test report covering normal and failure paths
    • AI evaluation results against agreed acceptance thresholds
    • Staged launch plan with rollback
    • Runbook and operator training

    What we need from you

    • Operators available for acceptance testing
    • Sign-off from the operations and CX owners
    • An agreed launch window outside sale events
  5. 05

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    Operate & improve

    After launch we watch the numbers with you: RTO, NDR resolution, handoff rates, opt-outs and failures. Monthly reviews retire messages that do not earn their place, update knowledge sources when policies change, and prepare the stack before sale events.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly KPI and exception review
    • Template, rule and knowledge-base updates
    • Sale-event readiness checklist
    • Change log and access review

    What we need from you

    • A named owner for each live automation
    • Advance notice of policy, pricing or channel changes
    • Feedback from agents and operators

Suggested first pilot

COD confirmation and failed-delivery resolution pilot

A focused four-week pilot on one storefront and one courier aggregator: WhatsApp confirmation for COD and flagged orders, a review queue for held orders, and NDR follow-up before the courier cut-off. Results are compared with a holdout group of orders, so both teams can see what changed before scaling.

  • One storefront or OMS and one courier aggregator connected
  • COD and address confirmation on WhatsApp with SMS or IVR fallback
  • Risk rules and a review queue for held and high-value orders
  • NDR follow-up loop with reattempt instructions sent back to the courier
  • Holdout-based report on confirmation, NDR resolution and RTO

Governance

Safe by design, owned by your team.

  • Consent first: every marketing message checks a recorded opt-in for that channel and purpose, and opt-outs sync across WhatsApp, SMS and email tools within an agreed time.
  • People decide money matters: refunds, cancellations, price changes, retailer credit and claim outcomes are approved by named roles. AI drafts, summarizes and flags only.
  • Grounded AI: assistants answer only from approved policies, catalogs and order data, cite their source, refuse medical or safety advice, and are scored on sampled conversations every week.
  • Honest design: discount, urgency and stock messages are reviewed against the CCPA dark-pattern guidelines, and every announced discount carries a traceable prior price.
  • Data minimization and security: card data stays within the payment gateway's PCI DSS-scoped systems, partners see only what a job needs, access is role-based and logged, and retention is agreed per data type.
  • Change control: every template, rule and prompt change is versioned, tested in staging and approved by its owner before going live, with a rollback path.

Compliance notes

The obligations that shape the design.

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 and the 2026 amendment

E-commerce entities must show seller, total price, return, refund, warranty and delivery terms, record explicit consent rather than pre-ticked boxes, and acknowledge complaints within 48 hours and resolve them within a month. An amendment notified in 2026 and applying from January 1, 2027 adds prior-price display for announced discounts, labeled sponsored listings, importer and country-of-origin details and a yearly dark-pattern self-audit.

pib.gov.in · Source ↗

CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

The guidelines specify 13 dark patterns, including false urgency, basket sneaking, confirm shaming, forced action, subscription traps, drip pricing and nagging, and the CCPA advised platforms in 2025 to self-audit. Cart recovery, stock and countdown messages, subscription cancellation and fee disclosure are designed to avoid them.

ccpa.doca.gov.in · Source ↗

Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 and category rules

E-commerce entities must display the declarations required on the package on the listing itself, such as manufacturer, packer or importer, net quantity, MRP inclusive of taxes, country of origin and consumer care details. Changes first proposed in November 2025 add a searchable country-of-origin filter for imported goods; we track the notified start date. Category rules add more, such as FSSAI license and label details for food and BIS hallmarking with HUID for gold jewelry.

consumeraffairs.nic.in · Source ↗

Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025

Consent notices must itemize the personal data and purpose, withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent, and security safeguards and breach notification are required. E-commerce entities with at least two crore registered users in India must erase data after three years of inactivity, with 48 hours' notice. Most obligations apply from May 2027 under the notified schedule; we design to them now. GDPR-style rules apply in parallel for EU and UK shoppers.

meity.gov.in · Source ↗

WhatsApp Business Messaging and Commerce Policies

Businesses may message only people who shared their number and opted in, must use approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window, must offer a clear path to a human when automating, and must not ask for full card or ID numbers in chat. Catalogs follow the WhatsApp Commerce Policy, which restricts some product categories, and template messages are charged per delivered message by category.

business.whatsapp.com · Source ↗

TRAI TCCCPR rules for SMS and voice

Commercial SMS and calls in India run through registered headers and content templates on the DLT platform, carry the right category and respect DND preferences and recorded consent. Order, delivery and warranty updates are service messages; offers are promotional and must carry an opt-out. A Third Amendment notified in September 2026 further revises the consent provisions, so templates are checked against the current text.

trai.gov.in · Source ↗

Questions

Frequently asked.

Do we need to replace Shopify, Unicommerce or our helpdesk?

No. We build around the systems you already run, using their official APIs and webhooks. Where a channel has no API, as with some quick-commerce partner portals, we use scheduled file uploads with checks. New tools are added only where they fill a clear gap, such as a review console or a data warehouse.

Can you send WhatsApp messages to all our past customers?

Only to people who gave you their number and opted in to hear from you on WhatsApp, for the kinds of messages they agreed to. Outside the 24-hour customer service window, every message must use an approved template. We help you design opt-in at checkout and on your site, and keep order updates separate from marketing so shoppers can choose.

Will an AI bot decide refunds or cancel orders?

No. AI drafts answers from your approved policies, summarizes claims and flags risky orders. Refunds, cancellations, replacements, price changes and retailer credit are decided by named people on your team, through review queues we build for them.

Is AI-assisted support still allowed on WhatsApp after Meta's 2026 terms change?

Meta's Business Solution terms restrict general-purpose AI assistants offered as the main product, not businesses using AI for their own customer support, order tracking or FAQs. Our assistants are scoped to your store, answer from your sources and hand over to people. We review the current terms with you during Design, because Meta decides how they apply.

How do you handle the dark-pattern guidelines and the new prior-price rule?

We review every discount, urgency and stock message against the CCPA guidelines before launch: no fake timers, no pre-added items, fees shown upfront, and canceling as easy as signing up. For announced discounts, the price sync keeps a dated price history so the prior price can be shown as the amended E-Commerce Rules require from January 1, 2027.

How soon will we see something working?

A focused pilot such as COD confirmation and failed-delivery resolution is planned for about four weeks from kickoff, including template approval and testing. Larger programs, such as multi-channel stock sync or a support assistant, are planned in phases of a few weeks each, with a working increment at the end of every phase.

What does it cost to run once it is live?

Running costs depend on your volumes. Meta charges per delivered WhatsApp template message, at rates set by category and country in its rate card; free-form replies inside the 24-hour customer service window are currently not charged. Add SMS, AI model usage and hosting. We model these during Design so you can see the running cost per order before you commit.

We also sell internationally. Does this work outside India?

Yes. The same flows work for international stores, with GDPR-style consent and data rights for EU and UK shoppers, EU rules on showing the prior price of a discount, local email and SMS marketing rules, and Stripe or a local gateway for payments. Indian rules such as Legal Metrology and TRAI DLT registration apply to Indian sales and messaging.
